description: Flat 8 m square of unmarked asphalt carriageway -- one quad, one seamless PBR texture set, tiling in both axes with no markings and no sidewalk.

image.prompt:
A SEAMLESSLY TILING TOP-DOWN GROUND TEXTURE. This is a flat material swatch, not a photograph of a scene or of an object. The camera looks straight down at the ground from directly overhead, perfectly orthographic, with no perspective, no horizon, no vanishing point and no tilt.

The surface: Flat square of plain unmarked asphalt road surface seen as a single unbroken sheet, no lane markings, no kerb, no sidewalk, no drains and no covers, edge to edge asphalt only Materials: Seamlessly tiling patched grey-black asphalt, coarse aggregate showing through worn binder, dark tar crack seams and rectangular pothole patches of a slightly different tone, faint tyre-polish lanes, thin dust and oil spotting, no paint of any kind; the pattern must wrap on all four edges so that any edge meets any other edge with no visible join.

Scale: the square shown covers exactly 8 by 8 metres of real ground, so every stone, block, slab, joint, marking, rut and tuft in it is drawn at its true size relative to that. Do not zoom in on a detail and do not pull back to show a wider scene.

Tiling: the texture must repeat seamlessly on all four edges. What runs off the left edge continues onto the right edge, and what runs off the top continues onto the bottom, exactly. No feature may be cut in half at an edge without its other half appearing at the opposite edge. Laid out four by four this must read as one continuous surface with no visible grid, no repeated landmark feature and no seam.

Framing: the surface fills the entire frame edge to edge and corner to corner. There is no border, no frame, no margin, no backdrop, no background, no matte and no empty space of any kind. The ground continues past every edge of the image.

Nothing stands on it and nothing bounds it: no kerb, no wall, no step, no gutter, no drain, no manhole cover, no grass verge, no plants, no people, no vehicles, no furniture, no objects, no litter, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows.

Lighting: flat, even, shadowless overhead illumination, like a lightbox. The image is the surface's true albedo. No sun, no cast shadows, no directional highlights, no specular blowout, no vignette, no gradient across the frame, no baked ambient occlusion in the corners and crevices, no light falloff towards the edges -- an uneven frame cannot tile, because its bright side would meet its dark side at every seam.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, realistic material, real surface wear and staining. Not stylised, not cartoon, not a 3D render preview, not a tiled collage of separate photographs, not a pattern illustration.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

notes: One flat quad, 8 x 8 m, lying in the ground plane at y=0 -- two triangles, one geometry, one draw call, one PBR material, and nothing else. The whole surface reads out of the texture; nothing is modelled. This is the base piece of a DECOMPOSED road kit: the carriageway carries no sidewalk at all, and the sidewalk is a separate placeable strip (Concrete Sidewalk Strip, 2.0 m wide and 0.15 m tall). Splitting them is the entire point of this set -- a builder puts a sidewalk down one side, both sides or neither, and nothing inside the road texture has to line up with anything inside the sidewalk texture, which is the alignment problem this replaces. The contract is: 8 x 8 m footprint on the kit's 8 m grid, pivot base-center so tiles snap on 8 m centres, and the asphalt tiles SEAMLESSLY in both axes. That makes the piece fully four-way rotationally symmetric -- it drops in at any of four orientations and any edge mates with any edge of any other asphalt tile in the set, including the lane-marked one, whose asphalt base must be the same tone and grain. Budget overridden explicitly to 2 triangles / 1 draw call / 1 material / 1 unique geometry instead of the hero2x its 8 m footprint would derive: footprint drives the class, but there is no geometry here to spend a class budget on. Quality comes entirely from a high-end tiling PBR texture -- albedo, roughness, normal and AO -- and not from mesh detail; that is the whole bet of this piece. It will be instanced more heavily than anything else in the kit, forty on screen at once being normal, so one shared geometry and one shared material collapse under an InstancedMesh. Manhole covers and drain grates are deliberately NOT in this texture: they are separate small props (Cast Iron Manhole Cover, Kerbside Storm Drain Grate) dropped on top wherever wanted, so the asphalt stays a pure repeat. No destruction groups: a road tile is static level geometry, not a breakable. Note for anyone mixing sets: the kit's older road-straight-tile and road-drain-and-utility-tile bake a 1.25 m FLAT sidewalk band into the road texture and are a different, incompatible family -- do not run them in the same street as this one.
